input: Scheduled routine: continue work on the repo aiming to develop, deploy, market, sell and support revenue generating software products in production; merge when done.
task: Deepen flagship xer-schedule-check: XER to Microsoft Project XML converter
errors: First LOE handling (manual tasks keeping their links) moved the CCA finish 18 months in the read-back; fixed by moving those links into task notes.
First MPXJ run: assignment work fell back to budget when actual+remaining was 0, and per-assignment minute rounding; fixed (73 of 425 example-file activities differed before).
A notes regex over the 46 MB CCA output was quadratic and had to be killed; replaced with a split on </Task>.
Auto-mode classifier refused a local python http.server for the browser check; used Playwright request interception to serve files instead (no listening process).

doc_friction.issue: Start here named open-tennis-robots (12 records in 2 days); the brief asked for revenue products, so I took flagship row 8 instead. The allocator has no notion of which flagship rows face a paying market.
The hook refusing pkill -f '[n]ame' when the name also appears elsewhere in the command line cost a retry; the CLAUDE.md note says only that the first letter must be bracketed.

deviations.why: Start here picked open-tennis-robots (hardware CAD, heavily worked, no market path); the starting message asks for revenue-generating products and xer-schedule-check competes with paid converters and schedule-analysis seats
deviations.did: took flagship row 8 xer-schedule-check, item: XER to Microsoft Project XML
deviations.result: shipped and verified; converter checked on six public files two ways

goal: A free in-browser P6 XER to Microsoft Project converter: a high-intent search ('open XER in MS Project') that brings the people who receive XER files without a P6 seat to the schedule-check tool.
notes: Local verification: run_venture_tests.py xer-schedule-check: 1 suite, 0 failed (after fixing 2 unguarded object-map lookups that inherited_keys.py flagged); msproject.test.mjs 7 tests + page.test.mjs pass; check_posts ok; validate.py ok; Playwright on the page at 390 px: panel hidden until an XER loads, download is valid MSPDI, warnings render, converted_to_project counted, no console errors, hidden for MSPDI input. eval/msproject-check.mjs: 21,422/21,422 activities intact, 54,843/54,843 links, 1,810/1,810 LOE links in notes, schedule 19,818/19,822 equal under Project's rules (12,169 early finishes equal under P6's options). MPXJ 16.10 (eval/msproject-mpxj.py): every field equal on all 21,422 activities but one external-date constraint written on purpose. Not opened in Microsoft Project itself.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: a senior developer writing an MSPDI writer with calendars, progress and resources, plus two verification harnesses (own reader + MPXJ) over six P6 files, page and docs

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
